title: The Wolf and the Sheep
attribution: Excerpted verbatim from Aesop's Fables, translated by V. S. Vernon Jones (1912), via Project Gutenberg.
body: A Wolf was worried and badly bitten by dogs, and lay a long time for dead. By and by he began to revive, and, feeling very hungry, called out to a passing Sheep and said, "Would you kindly bring me some water from the stream close by? I can manage about meat, if only I could get something to drink." But this Sheep was no fool. "I can quite understand", said he, "that if I brought you the water, you would have no difficulty about the meat. Good-morning."

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what happened to the Wolf at the start of the passage?
options: He was worried and badly bitten by dogs
He fell into a deep pit
He lost a fight with another wolf
He was caught in a hunter's trap

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Wolf do once he began to revive?
options: He called out to a passing Sheep
He limped away to find shelter
He searched for the dogs that bit him
He fell back asleep from exhaustion

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what did the Wolf ask the Sheep to bring him?
options: Some water from the stream close by
A piece of meat from the flock
Bandages for his wounds
Help from the shepherd

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Wolf say he can manage on his own?
options: The meat, if only he had something to drink
The walk back to his den
Finding water himself, eventually
Fighting off the dogs again

questions.prompt: According to the passage, how is the Sheep described when the Wolf makes his request?
options: As no fool
As easily frightened
As too far away to hear him
As sympathetic to the Wolf's pain

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what does the Sheep say would happen if he brought the Wolf water?
options: The Wolf would have no difficulty about the meat
The Wolf would immediately recover and run off
The Wolf would thank him and leave in peace
The dogs would return and attack them both

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "worried" mean in "A Wolf was worried and badly bitten by dogs"?
options: Concerned or anxious
Attacked and harassed
Confused and lost
Warned in advance

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, why does the Sheep refuse to fetch the water?
options: He understands that helping the Wolf recover would only let it eat him afterward
He does not know where the stream is located
He believes the Wolf is not actually injured
He is too weak himself to make the trip

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what condition was the Wolf left in after being bitten by dogs?
options: He lay a long time for dead
He was left with only minor scratches
He was chased far from his usual territory
He lost his sense of smell

questions.prompt: According to the passage, what exact word does the Sheep use to end the conversation?
options: "Good-morning"
"Farewell forever"
"Never again"
"Not today"

questions.prompt: According to the passage, why did the Wolf call out to the Sheep in the first place?
options: He was feeling very hungry after beginning to revive
He wanted directions back to his den
He wanted the Sheep to warn other wolves
He wanted company while he recovered

questions.prompt: As the passage uses it, what does "revive" mean in "he began to revive"?
options: To regain strength or consciousness
To fall into a deeper sleep
To become more badly injured
To run away in fear

questions.prompt: Based on the passage, what is the flaw in the Wolf's request that the Sheep sees through?
options: The Wolf's plea for water conceals his real plan to eat the Sheep once he has recovered
The Wolf actually has plenty of water nearby already
The Wolf is lying about having been bitten by dogs
The Wolf wants the Sheep to fetch the dogs instead

questions.prompt: Which of these best summarizes what happens in the passage?
options: An injured Wolf asks a Sheep to fetch water, but the Sheep refuses, seeing that it would only help the Wolf recover enough to eat him
A Wolf and a Sheep share a stream of water together
A Sheep brings water to an injured Wolf out of pity
A Wolf recovers fully before ever meeting the Sheep
